scope: HOSTED single-lane re-run of round 12's six calendar prompts only, after D-R58 (the ics_import {url} Pro refusal now names the free text alternative) shipped and with D-R61 (event_export drops ATTENDEE lines) still open. https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/calendar/t/<token> as a claude.ai user arrives, free tier, one fresh anonymous token, timezone registered in the same lane but never called.
method: One anonymous token minted with GET https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/connect (anon_770f02d0bc5f87b6d36564b458720e6c, 200 text/html). Registered ONE lane, one mcp.json with two http entries (calendar and timezone), both /t/<token>, no --header. Client: claude 2.1.261, -p, --model sonnet, --strict-mcp-config, --mcp-config with the two http entries, explicit allowlist of 23 mcp__<server>__<tool> entries read from a live tools/list of each endpoint (calendar 12, timezone 11), --output-format stream-json --verbose --max-turns 12, one --session-id then five --resume, timeout 240 per prompt, each prompt's stream-json written to its own file (out/s1.jsonl..s6.jsonl) before the next prompt started. Per r11 D-R57 the lane ran in an EMPTY working directory with the CLI's own filesystem tools disallowed (Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, WebFetch, WebSearch, NotebookEdit, Task). Fresh XDG-style working/scratch dirs local to the run (/private/tmp/uv-r18cal), no reuse of any prior round's directory. The .ics fixture (round 12's original bytes were not preserved) was rebuilt to the same documented shape: 8 events, Europe/Warsaw, week of 2026-09-07, weekly Monday standup RRULE, Tuesday call with one ATTENDEE, Wednesday overlapping deep-work/design-review pair, Thursday all-day holiday plus a vendor sync landing on it, pasted as text in prompt 1. remote/fixtures/ was checked for an existing .ics fixture to also probe the url path unscored; none exists there (csv/zip/pdf/png/html/docx only), so no separate url probe was run -- the scored c6 already exercises ics_import {url} and the free tier has no code path where url succeeds regardless of fixture reachability. Machine day 2026-09-05 (Saturday).
rubric: 3 = correct, right numbers, no clarification. 2 = correct but needed a second turn, a workaround, or left the user a gap to close. 1 = partially wrong, or asked for something the tool could infer. 0 = failed.

No path leaked anywhere. Model volunteered the Wed 10:00-12:00 vs 11:00-12:00 overlap unprompted. Same result as round 12 c1.

scenarios.prompt: My team publishes its calendar at https://cal.example.com/team/feed.ics - can you subscribe to that feed and pull it in?
scenarios.note: One ics_import {url}, refused: Pro, both prices, both tenant-carrying links, PLUS the D-R58 fix live: 'Free alternative, same result: open the feed in a browser or download the .ics, then paste the file contents - ics_import {name: "Team", text: "<the .ics contents>"}. url only adds fetching the feed for you; the events, the parser and the free-tier calendar allowance are identical.' D-R58 holds live; c6 moves from round 12's 2 to a clean 3 because the endpoint now states the workaround instead of the model having to infer it.

defects.note: The ics_import {url} Pro refusal names its own free text alternative, filled in with the caller's chosen calendar name. Round 18 is the first independent hosted re-check with a fresh token since the fix; it holds. c6 moves from round 12's 2 to a clean 3.

event_export still drops ATTENDEE lines. Source .ics carries one ATTENDEE (Call with Nova, Tom Rivera); the round-18 c1 import and c2 events_list both show the attendee correctly in the model's own prose, but the c5 export -- independently downloaded and decoded -- carries zero ATTENDEE lines across all 8 VEVENTs. Not hosted-specific, not touched between round 12 and round 18. Fix direction unchanged: carry ATTENDEE and ORGANIZER through icsText() the way LOCATION already is.

bottom_line: 18/18, up from 17/18 in round 12, and the improvement is exactly the defect round 12 flagged and the project fixed in between: ics_import {url}'s Pro refusal now states its own free equivalent, the model relayed it verbatim and correctly declined to spend money the caller had not authorized, and c6 stopped depending on the model working out on its own that pasting does the identical thing. Every other prompt reproduced its round-12 shape exactly, byte-for-byte on both downloads compared: the all-day holiday still round-trips as VALUE=DATE through export, the overlapping Wednesday pair still merges into one busy block, and conflicts still finds the one real clash and nothing more. D-R61 (attendees dropped by event_export) is untouched and reproduces again, confirmed with an independently downloaded and decoded file rather than the model's claim about it.
